A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the in-medium properties of charmonium resonances are essential for understanding charmonium production and dissociation in heavy-ion collisions, and that a consistent description of the available experimental data requires an in-medium reduction of charmonium masses and widths.
a realistic description of the in-medium properties of charmonia is mandatory to understand the observed suppression pattern.
the in-medium properties of hidden-charm states are crucial for a consistent description of charmonium production at finite temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the J/psi suppression observed in heavy-ion collisions can be explained by the hadronic phase only, while the charmonium production at high temperatures is dominated by the plasma.
a detailed description of the in-medium modifications of the open and hidden-charm sectors is essential for a consistent interpretation of charmonium production data in heavy-ion collisions.
the J/psi suppression observed in heavy-ion collisions at the SPS can be explained by a combination of inelastic hadronic interactions and recombination of charm quarks.
